metadata.title: U.S. chip stocks slide as traders unwind Nvidia rival bets before earnings

content.text:
Investing.com -- U.S. chip stocks are down sharply on Monday as traders took profits on recent gains in Nvidia's rivals ahead of the AI giant's earnings, while worries about tighter export controls added to the pressure.
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) fell 7.3%, and Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) dropped 7.1%. Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) lost 5.9%, Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) slid 4.8% and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) dropped over 5%.
AMD rose last week after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's exit, as traders bet it could take market share from Nvidia. Investors are now unwinding those positions ahead of Nvidia's results on Tuesday. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) has declined a more modest 1.9% to $159.70.
Export controls may have added to concerns. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for tighter enforcement of chip export controls to China on Sunday and gave Nvidia's board a 10-day deadline to show compliance.
"I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel," Bessent said in a Sunday television appearance.
The Nasdaq is down 1.9%, and the S&P 500 has dropped 1.2% so far on Monday, as tech and chip stocks lead losses.
